clauses: whether immediate invention may occur before Economy
answers.answer: Turns 1–5 proceed Trade → Economy → Confluence, with sharing then colony bids then research-team bids in Confluence. Trade ends when all but one player are done. Players may immediately invent after a trade or use other Trade abilities before their Economy.

evidence.text: Players act simultaneously within phases; bidding resolves in ranked order. **Turns 1–5 follow Trade → Economy → Confluence: first share technologies, then colony bids, then research-team bids.** The detailed sequence is:

Trade resources, ships, cards and promises during Trade only. All parties must agree to everything before a trade happens. Multilateral trades and trades contingent on another trade are binding, as are promises for later in this turn or future turns. No player may intentionally withhold agreed goods.

During Trade, run the violet converter on a research team you control. Pay **one complete alternative input set** shown to the left of its arrow (not all alternatives together). Take its printed invention points, flip the research team to its invented side, and immediately put your matching species card from your library into play. Do not yet take the Sharing Bonus. The converter preview on a research card shows the general effect; actual resource colors can differ by species.

answers.answer: The player must perform as much of the agreement as possible, then lose 7 points: 2 for the missing card, 2 for the octagon, 2 for the two cubes, and 1 for the ship. The score can go negative.

evidence.text: If a promise becomes impossible, everyone involved may agree on compensation. If they do not, the offender must perform as much of the original agreement as possible, then lose **2 points for each missing card, octagon or promised point**, and **1 point for each missing cube or ship**. These losses can make the offender's score negative.

answers.answer: The species-background card is a loan and returns at turn end. The colony and research team have no player background and transfer permanently.

evidence.text: A card with its owner's species background is loaned only until the end of the turn and must return then. Cards without player backgrounds, including colonies and research teams, transfer permanently. Trade ends when all but one player are done. Players may immediately invent or use other Trade abilities before running their Economy. Avoid discussing potential trades outside Trade, except the limited bid negotiation below.

answers.answer: During Trade, run the controlled research team’s violet converter and pay one complete alternative input set shown to the left of the arrow. Take its invention points, flip the team, and immediately put the inventor’s matching species card into play. Other players normally put matching cards into play at Confluence after that Economy; the inventor receives no Sharing Bonus at invention, and each invention earns the current Confluence Sharing Bonus then.

evidence.text: During Trade, run the violet converter on a research team you control. Pay **one complete alternative input set** shown to the left of its arrow (not all alternatives together). Take its printed invention points, flip the research team to its invented side, and immediately put your matching species card from your library into play. Do not yet take the Sharing Bonus. Gain the current Confluence card's **upper-left Sharing Bonus for each invention**; Yengii instead uses its upper-right Yengii bonus. clauses: named-card upgrade ownership and in-play requirements
answers.answer: Both cards must be in play and held by their own owner, not loaned out. Put the spent card underneath the flipped target. A renamed upgraded card loses its old identity, so it cannot pay an upgrade requiring its former name.

evidence.text: Most cards offer two alternative ways to upgrade. Either pay the printed violet upgrade converter, taking any other output and flipping the card, or spend the named card printed as an alternative. For the named-card route, **both cards must be in play and held by their own owner, not loaned out**. Flip the target and put the spent card underneath it. Each card may be spent for only one upgrade. A renamed upgraded card no longer has its original identity: Genetic Resynthesis, for example, cannot pay an upgrade requiring Genetic Engineering. A hidden spent card is not another available copy.

clauses: whether white converter can be skipped or run twice
answers.answer: At the beginning of Economy, discard excess colonies beneath the colony deck before production. White economic converters are optional and normally run at most once per turn, so one can be skipped but not ordinarily run twice. Converters run simultaneously, so one converter’s output cannot fund another in that Economy.

evidence.text: At the **beginning of Economy**, check your current Colony Support. Put excess colonies beneath the colony deck before production. Support is not checked when bidding or trading: you can acquire excess colonies and sell or consume them before the check.

Each white economic converter is optional and normally runs at most once per turn. A converter with no input produces for free. Pay its actual complete inputs to receive its output. All economic converters run simultaneously: **no output of one economic converter can fund another in that same Economy**, including points and ships. A useful procedure is to place preexisting goods on chosen inputs, place new goods from the pool on outputs, then return spent goods to the pool. Do not negotiate or speak with other players until everyone finishes production. Explicit species exceptions, such as Caylion seedling colonies, override the once-per-turn limit.

answers.answer: Keep donation output in the donation area until traded or gifted. During the next Trade, trade all of it away and give away anything still there at Trade’s end. Players cannot refuse a gift, and donation victory points can be traded.

evidence.text: The hand symbol with a violet outline marks donation resources, ships or points. Put them in your donation area and leave them there until traded or gifted. During the **next Trade**, trade all such goods away; give away any still there at the end of that Trade. Players cannot refuse a gift. Donation victory points are the exception to ordinary points being untradable. In the **last Economy**, the producer keeps all donation output instead.

clauses: five-ship bid purchase cost for minimum-two colony
answers.answer: After sharing, secretly divide ships into colony bid, research-team bid, and retained ships; commit both bids before revealing either. Resolve colony bids highest to lowest, then research-team bids. A successful five-ship bid spends all five ships even if the card’s minimum is two. evidence.text: After sharing, announce your total ships. Secretly divide them into a colony bid, a research-team bid and retained ships behind your screen. Any pile may be empty. Commit both bids before revealing either: put the two bids in separate closed fists; retained ships stay hidden until bidding finishes.

Reveal colony bids simultaneously. From highest to lowest, each player may buy **one** colony or pass, except Kjas split bids. To buy, your effective bid must meet the colony's printed minimum; spend **all the ships committed to that purchase**, not just the minimum. If you pass, keep your bid; if no legal card remains, you must pass. You may buy even if it exceeds Colony Support, which is checked only next Economy.

Then reveal and resolve research-team bids by the same purchase/pass procedure. For equal bids, the player with **fewer cards of the type being bid on** chooses first; if still tied, the **higher printed species tiebreak** chooses first. Count colonies for colony bids and research teams for research bids, not all economic cards. Kt’Zr’Kt’Rtl has special colony-tie priority and an infinite final tiebreak; Yengii invented technologies do not count as research teams against them.

**Seedlings.** Put a ×2 seedling token on Caylion's starting colony and on any colony Caylion takes from the colony bid track. Do not add one merely because another player trades a colony to Caylion. clauses: whether Eni Et may run own interest converters
whether Eni Et may upgrade them
answers.answer: Eni Et cannot run their own interest converters, including upgraded ones, but may upgrade them and loan them to others. The borrower’s output is the same large Unity wild plus three blue large cubes.

evidence.text: **Interest converters.** An interest converter accepts a single color and outputs that same color, within the printed sizes/quantities. **Eni Et cannot run their own interest converters**, including upgraded ones, but may upgrade the cards and loan them to others. Upgraded interest converters retain these rules even when their output does not exceed input. Unlike Unity or Zeth wild selections, Eni Et's wild resources on a card must match.

**Unity wild inputs.** Gray wilds can be included with same-sized input cubes of one color. They are not destroyed: move those exact wilds from input to output, then fill the remainder of the printed output with cubes of that one matching color/size. With only wild input, choose a single appropriate-sized ordinary color for the remaining output. Interest converters never create additional wilds. For a 2-to-4 large-cube interest converter fed one blue and one large wild, output is that same wild plus three blue cubes.

**Protection Racket.** Zeth cannot steal from anyone it traded with during the previous Trade Phase. Use Safe/Vulnerable markers to track this. Donation goods **can** be offered in an explicitly declared trade to Zeth, who may accept or refuse it; an accepted trade provides protection.

Yes. Apply the original Steal Phase as the **last action before counting score**, after final sharing.
